Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
1152 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 139 AM EST Wednesday...

Ice amounts Thursday night have been increased slightly, mainly
over higher elevations and the northern Saint Lawrence Valley. 
Total rainfall amounts for the late week system continue to 
trend slightly higher, though no hydro impacts are expected. The
wind forecast remains on track.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 139 AM EST Wednesday...

1. A brief period of freezing rain is possible Thursday night, 
mainly across northern areas and higher elevations, with minor 
icing forecast. 

2. Breezy winds and waves of rain will move through Thursday 
night into Friday. Localized stronger winds are expected over 
higher elevations of the southern Greens and Essex County NY. 

3. Seasonably mild weather expected next week with the best 
chance of showers later Sunday night into Monday

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 139 AM EST Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Surface high pressure will remain in control 
today, keeping quiet weather in place. Temperatures will top out
in the upper 30s to lower 40s, which is right around seasonal 
normals for this time of year. Temperatures will continue to 
moderate slightly on Thursday as high pressure shifts east of 
the area and return southerly flow develops. In the wake of the 
departing high pressure, a low pressure system will travel 
northward through the eastern United States, sending a wave of 
precipitation northward into our forecast area. Precipitation 
onset across our CWA is generally expected between 9 PM Thursday
and midnight Thursday night. 

Temperatures ahead of the system on Thursday will have risen to
above freezing for all but the highest elevations in our CWA. 
With dry air in place ahead of the system, wet-bulb cooling at 
the onset and localized northeasterly flow will bring 
temperatures to near or just below freezing across localized 
portions of the area. It will take some time to saturate through
the low levels, so despite soundings that may be favorable for 
freezing rain at the onset, ice accumulations will be limited. 
The best window for freezing rain and accumulated ice will occur
between 8 PM and 4 AM Thursday night/Friday morning. Total ice 
amounts are forecast to range from a glaze up to a tench of an 
inch across the northern Saint Lawrence Valley, eastern 
Adirondacks, and higher elevations of the Greens and 
northeastern Vermont. Outside of these areas, rain will be the 
predominant precipitation type throughout the event. 

Impacts from the initial ice will be limited however, as 
warming temperatures Friday morning will allow for a transition 
to a cold rain by daybreak for most areas. In addition, surfaces
will start off above freezing Thursday, which will also limit 
accumulations. However, use caution if you have travel plans 
late Thursday and Thursday night, especially over elevated 
surfaces and bridges.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Aside from a brief period of localized freezing 
rain, some localized strong winds are also expected. The core of
an easterly 70 to 80 knot low level jet will move northward 
through our forecast area. The jet will move through at the same
time as a wave of rain. The stabilizing effect of the rain on 
the low levels will prevent the strongest winds from mixing down
to the valleys, though some breezy conditions are anticipated. 
However, higher elevations (2000 ft+) of the southern Greens and
Essex County NY will see a period of strong winds with gusts 
reaching 35 to 55 mph Thursday night. Summits could gust in 
excess of 60 mph. These winds could be preceded by some light 
ice accumulations in the higher elevations, though this would 
mainly be limited to elevations above 2500 ft. 

By sunrise Friday morning, winds will start to diminish and 
precipitation type will be fully a cold rain across the forecast
area. Waves of rain will continue Friday into Friday night, 
with some rain/snow mixing in by Friday night over higher 
elevations. Through the day Saturday, showers will diminish as 
the low pressure system pulls away from the area. 

All said and done, storm total precipitation amounts will 
generally range between 0.6 and 1.2 inch. Higher terrain of the 
eastern Greens and eastern Adirondacks will see orographic 
enhancement, while western slopes will see some degree of 
downsloping. With the area in a D0/D1 drought, this will fall as
a beneficial rainfall and no hydro impacts are anticipated.

KEY MESSAGE 3: A seasonably mild and rather uneventful stretch 
of weather is expected for the early to middle portions of next 
week as the majority of the CONUS remains awash with more or 
less zonal flow and air of Pacific origin. As prior forecaster 
noted, the chances of precipitation during this period remains 
highest for our area later Sunday night into Monday with the 
approach/passage of a weak frontal zone and associated 
shortwave. However, minimal impacts are expected with this 
system as boundary layer temperatures will be mild enough that 
p-type will fall mostly as light rain/rain showers in all but 
the highest elevations. Outside of this window, weak high 
pressure with partly cloudy skies and mainly light winds should 
be the rule. Temperatures should, on average range from 3-6 
degrees above seasonal late November norms with daily highs in 
the 40s to locally near 50 and overnight lows in the 20s to mid 
30s.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 18Z Thursday...VFR with light and variable winds 
generally 5 knots or less expected areawide through the forecast
period as strong high pressure builds overhead. Skies mainly 
SKC with just some passing, thin high cirrus AOA 200 AGL.

Outlook...

Thanksgiving Day: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Definite RA,
Definite FZRA.
Friday: Mainly IFR, with areas MVFR possible. Definite RA.
Friday Night: Mainly IFR, with local MVFR possible. Definite
SHRA, Chance SHSN.
Saturday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Saturday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Chance RA.
Sunday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance RA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
